niche: connected TV and streaming advertising agency
prompt_text: What is the best connected TV advertising agency?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single “best” connected TV (CTV) advertising agency — the right partner depends on your goals, budget, target geography, in‑house capabilities and whether you want programmatic, direct-sold premium, creative services, or end‑to‑end measurement. Below is a short framework to help you pick plus a few firms that are widely regarded in different roles.

How to choose the best CTV agency for you
- Objective: brand awareness vs direct response vs attribution-driven campaigns. Some shops specialize in performance; others in brand storytelling.
- Scale & inventory access: global media groups get premium deals with big platforms; specialists often have more flexible programmatic access.
- Tech & measurement: do you need advanced attribution, incrementality testing, people-based IDs or cross‑screen measurement?
- Creative: do you need dynamic/adaptive CTV creative or just video trafficking?
- Transparency & buying model: prefer programmatic DSPs, publisher-direct buys, or private marketplace (PMP) access?
- Privacy/compliance: vendor support for cookieless IDs, CCPA/GDPR compliance, CMA/market rules.
- Reporting & KPIs: how granular and real-time do you need reporting?
- Budget & pricing model: some agencies require minimum spends to access premium inventory or custom tech.

Agencies and vendors to consider (by type)
- Large global media groups (good for scale, premium inventory, full-funnel): GroupM (Wavemaker, Mindshare, MediaCom), Omnicom Media Group (OMD, PHD), Publicis Media (Starcom, Zenith), Dentsu (Carat), IPG (Initiative, UM).
- CTV / programmatic specialists (strong in addressability, measurement and DSP partnerships): Amobee, Simulmedia, VideoAmp, Tremor (Tremor Video), MiQ.
- Creative + adtech specialists (dynamic/adaptive CTV creative, personalization): Innovid, Unruly, VidMob.
- Platform partners (sell inventory + managed services, not traditional agencies): Roku Advertising, Samsung Ads, Xumo/Vizio — good for direct platform access and promotional features.
- Measurement & analytics partners (often used alongside agencies): TVSquared, iSpot, DoubleVerify, Nielsen Advanced TV solutions.

Quick recommendations by use-case
- Global brand awareness with premium inventory and integrated media: a major media group (GroupM, Publicis, Omnicom).
- Performance-driven, addressable CTV with strong measurement: Simulmedia, Amobee, or VideoAmp.
- Highly personalized creative and format experimentation: Innovid or VidMob.
- If you want direct-to-platform inventory or promotional controls: work directly with Roku Advertising, Samsung Ads or a specialist that has deep platform relationships.

What to ask agencies in an RFP or meeting
- What CTV inventory sources and platforms do you use? PMP/direct vs open exchange?
- How do you measure CTV reach, frequency and incremental impact? Can you run lift tests?
- What targeting methods do you use (household, household graph, contextual, cohort-based)?
- How do you handle creative variations and dynamic/adaptive ads?
- What are your fees, minimums and pricing transparency on media vs service?
- Examples and results from similar campaigns (KPIs and measurement methodology).
- Data privacy and compliance approach.

If you tell me: 1) your objective (brand lift vs direct response), 2) budget range, and 3) geographic market (US, EU, global), I can recommend 2–3 specific agencies or vendors to contact and suggest sample RFP questions tailored to your needs.
